chapter_mission: Expose the group's philosophical fault lines. Torin's unsettling ease in a degraded Force zone; a three-cornered debate over the technique's nature; a small and quiet friendship forming between Kael and Desh. Per D7 counter-current 1, Torin does something a character on the corruption trajectory would genuinely not do — a small costless kindness whose register stays characterisation, not misdirection. Per W1 Inversion 1, Kael approaches Desh — not the Force-users — with a practical observation Desh had missed. The chapter surfaces problems the book will not solve until Parts 3 and 4.
chapter_turn: Ben notices Torin is comfortable where he should not be. He cannot yet name what it means, but the shape of it is filed — and Sera names it for him in a corridor, in private. Kael stops being the man who comments on the group's tensions and becomes the man who quietly makes himself useful to the one member who does not need the Force to be useful. The crew stops being 'the group we rescued' and starts being 'a coalition with visible fault lines.'

scene_plan.purpose: In transit through a moderately degraded zone. The Force stutters — presence flickering like a bad connection. Sera tightens. Kael goes still. Torin tilts his head and listens to the thinning, and something in his posture eases. He murmurs 'Ankhural called it the natural state' in a tone that isn't academic — it's nostalgic. After they clear the zone, Sera finds Ben in the corridor and grips his arm: 'Watch him. In the thin places. Watch what happens to his face.' H08 plants. The thin-place phenomenology at the moderate level uses force_mechanics.sensory_vocabulary.thin_places_moderate (PP17 atmospheric promise actively building). In the margins: Torin stops Kael in a narrow passage before Kael can clip his hip on a protruding bulkhead fitting — a small silent courtesy, not explained, not remarked on. Kael looks at him. Torin looks back. They move on. Per D7 counter-current 1: Torin doing something on the corruption trajectory he would genuinely not do — a costless protection of a man who will matter to the climax. Reads as characterisation, not plot signal.

The galley. Sera puts down her fork with precision that is itself a warning. Torin's reasonable hands on the table. Four positions surface: Sera (the Weave is sacred; the technique is violation), Torin (the Weave is structure; the technique is engineering), Kael (all three traditions built institutions around one answer and called that answer truth). Ben realises he does not have a position and tables the debate. Kael speaks last: 'You're all arguing about whose cage has nicer bars.' The silence after is the answer. Per D3 in-character variants: Sera uses 'the work,' Torin uses 'the stitching,' Kael uses 'the cloth' -- three different names for the same thing, each carrying its own theological commitments. Veraine's philosophy is present in the room as the unnamed fifth position: the seal as prison, release as mercy, cost accepted in advance.

Engineering crawlspace. Desh bangs on a conduit that has been cycling wrong since the extra passengers came aboard. Kael folds himself into the tight space beside him and begins handing tools without being asked. Per W1 Inversion 1: Kael has been watching the ship's systems. He has noticed a pattern Desh has not — a correlation between the Force-sensitives' proximity to certain bulkhead runs and the conduit's cycling errors. He offers the observation flatly, no framing. Short. Desh absorbs it. Moves on. He re-routes the conduit off the affected bulkhead path; the ship settles. Kael, watching Desh work: 'You don't feel any of it. The wrongness.' Desh: 'I feel the ship shaking and four Force-users arguing about why.' Kael almost smiles. Almost. Ben, passing through the corridor, registers from the side: an alliance he did not arrange. No narration underlines it. The reader holds it as texture.

relationship_turns.to: first philosophical fracture — the galley debate is the first time Sera visibly distrusts Torin's premises. She leaves the table without finishing. The wound they did not get to speak about in 1000 BBY is now a disagreement they are having in 47 ABY
private alliance — her warning in the corridor is the first thing she has trusted Ben with that is not the mission. Conditional, but real

relationship_turns.from: quiet alliance opened at Ch 7 margins
relationship_turns.to: first verified exchange — Kael's observation is accepted and acted on; Desh's dry response is the kind of registering that does not require acknowledgement. The hydrospanner passed in silence is the smallest handshake in the book. Both arcs register it differently; Ben observes without narrating

relationship_turns.from: rescued strangers on the same mission
relationship_turns.to: acknowledged — Torin's silent protection in the passage is seen by Kael, registered by Kael, unnamed by either. Per D7, this is counter-current, not misdirection; it will be one of the beats the Ch 15 private approach is built from.

exit_vector: Ship steady toward the next Corridor node. Torin's reasonable voice still in Ben's head. Sera's grip on his arm still in the muscle memory. Kael almost-smiling in the engineering bay behind Desh's shoulder. Nothing has changed tactically; everything has changed in the room.
notes: The chapter's register pivots between three sensibilities — Zahn for the transit opening, debate-drama precision for the galley, Allston-channel warmth for the engineering bay — and the pivots must feel earned, not whiplash. The galley debate is the highest-risk philosophical scene in the book; every line must move the conflict or reveal a speaker. No character should monologue. Kael's 'whose cage has nicer bars' is the chapter's exit line in the reader's memory — plant it and leave. Force phenomenology: moderate thin place in s1 (use force_mechanics.sensory_vocabulary.thin_places_moderate). Desh's environmental unease should register by instrument, not by intuition — chrono drift, a fitting that will not seal, a deck plate that sits one millimeter off true. ANTI-PATTERNS: (a) do not let Ben reach a position in s2 — his lack of position is the point; (b) do not make Torin explicitly quote Veraine's philosophy; Ankhural is enough; (c) Kael/Desh warmth must remain physical, not verbal — the hydrospanner does what words cannot; (d) per D7, the Torin passage-courtesy in s1 is rendered at ground level — a body noticing space and moving to protect another body. No narrator commentary that it is unusual or significant. It lives briefly and is not underlined. It must read as characterisation, not as 'is Torin really going to fall?' misdirection; (e) per W1 Plant 1 guardrails repeated for W1 Inversion 1, Kael's observation in s3 is not framed by his POV (he has none) nor by Ben's narration. Desh's response does the framing by accepting it. Ben registering from the side is a sentence of observation, not a paragraph of interpretation.
